japan1.title: 記録的水準の円安 今後は？暮らしはどうなる？【詳しく】

japan1.title: 5月の原油輸入量 前年比38％減 代替調達で4月より減少幅は縮小

bd3.title: CU admin identifies 2 molesters
bd3.description: The administration of Chittagong University yesterday claimed to have identified two persons who sexually assaulted a female student on the campus on Sunday night.

bd3.title: Rohingya genocide case to proceed
bd3.description: The World Court yesterday rejected Myanmar’s objections to a genocide case over its treatment of the Muslim Rohingya minority, paving the way for the case to be heard in full.

bd3.title: Need 1 week to assess situation
bd3.description: Admitting that the Power Division could not impose schedule-wise power cuts across the country, State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Nasrul Hamid yesterday sought one week’s time to address the issue.

bd3.title: Wasfia 1st Bangladeshi to conquer K2
bd3.description: Renowned Bangladeshi mountaineer Wasfia Nazreen conquered the treacherous K2 in Pakistan, becoming the first person from Bangladesh to summit the second-tallest mountain in the world.

bd3.title: CU sexual assault: Fingers pointed at BCL men
bd3.description: Those who sexually assaulted a female student on Chittagong University campus on July 17 night are members of Bangladesh Chhatra League, said police sources and CU BCL insiders.

bd3.title: Noab hikes newspaper price by Tk 2 from Jul 25
bd3.description: All newspapers owned by the members of Newspaper Owners’ Association of Bangladesh (Noab) will see a price increase of at least Tk 2 per issue from July 25.

bd3.title: Yet-to-start mega projects: Consider putting  them on hold
bd3.description: Given the current economic situation, the government should consider suspending mega projects the physical work of which has yet to begin, economist Debapriya Bhattacharya said yesterday.

bd3.title: ‘You cannot remain silent’
bd3.description: The High Court yesterday came down hard on Bangladesh Railway for mismanagement, ticket scalping and carrying passengers on the train roofs.

bd3.title: Electricity crisis may worsen
bd3.description: The government’s plan for one to two hours of daily power cuts is failing, especially in the north, and the signs are that the electricity crisis may worsen across the country in the coming days.

bd3.title: EC’s dialogue hits a snag as BNP skips it
bd3.description: The BNP yesterday skipped Election Commission’s dialogue seeking recommendations of political parties on how to hold a free and fair general election.

Canada Day activities in Ottawa cancelled due to 'extreme weather,' including fireworks
ca3.description: Evening Canada Day activities in Ottawa have been cancelled, including the fireworks display, due to "extreme weather," as flooding closed some streets in the city and thunderstorms led to power outages.

ca3.title: N.L. government declares fire ban for all Labrador, until at least July 13
ca3.description: The Minister of Forestry has ordered a blanket fire ban for Labrador, effective to at least July 13.

ca3.title: Teen driver charged after man on riding lawnmower killed in fatal collision in North Dumfries, Ont.
ca3.description: A 16-year-old has been charged with dangerous operation of a vehicle causing death, speeding and stunt driving after a fatal collision between a car and riding lawnmower last month. A 51-year-old North Dumfries Township man died in the collision.

ca3.title: Why one superfan thinks now is the right time for Canada's Eurovision debut
ca3.description: When it was announced that Canada would be entering the 2027 Eurovision Song Contest — it was music to Matti McLean’s ears. ca3.title: Canadians mark Canada Day as Carney urges unity, heat grips Central Canada
ca3.description: Officials in many provinces are urging people to stay hydrated and check on vulnerable neighbours as communities kick off celebrations for Canada's 159th birthday.

ca3.title: Canada will enter the 2027 Eurovision Song Contest
ca3.description: CBC/Radio-Canada and the European Broadcasting Union have announced Canada will participate in the 2027 Eurovision Song Contest in Bulgaria.

ca3.title: Application portal opens for $100 affordability payments for Albertans
ca3.description: Albertans can start applying today for $100 that the provincial government says is intended to help deal with the high cost of living.

ca3.title: I walked across Canada and it changed what I thought I knew about it
ca3.description: For most of her life, Sonya Richmond's understanding of Canada came from maps, media and flying quickly between major landmarks. That changed when she spent years walking across the country on the Trans Canada Trail.

ca3.title: N.L.'s loss, sacrifice at Beaumont-Hamel remembered on both sides of the Atlantic — 110 years later
ca3.description: More than a century after Newfoundland and Labrador soldiers far from home in northern France lost their lives, their sacrifice is still being honoured.

ca3.title: 2 legendary polar exploration shipwrecks are about to get their 21st-century close-up
ca3.description: An ambitious expedition will use Canadian technology to revisit two legendary polar exploration shipwrecks. The goal: create detailed digital twins of Quest and Terra Nova while leaving the historic wrecks undisturbed on the sea floor.

ca3.title: From Tamil to Cree to Mandarin, these stand-up comedians are using their mother tongue to land punchlines
ca3.description: Across Canada, a growing number of comedians are turning to their mother tongues on stage — not just as a stylistic choice, but as a way to tell more honest stories, reclaim histories shaped by migration and colonialism, and introduce audiences to perspectives not often heard.

ca3.title: B.C. says World Cup is boosting local economy, but some businesses report softer demand
ca3.description: As the FIFA World Cup passes its halfway mark, the B.C. government is touting the economic benefits of hosting the games in Vancouver but some local businesses say the boost has been uneven.

ca3.title: A slew of new laws are coming into effect in Ontario on Canada Day. Here's what you should know
ca3.description: July 1 marks the day when a host of regulatory and legal changes take effect. They include changes to landlord and tenants rules, auto insurance changes and expanded powers for pharmacists.

ca3.title: Does this N.S. town have the oldest Canada Day parade in the country?
ca3.description: The town of Westville has been celebrating July 1 since 1907 and is expecting around 12,000 people to take in the festivities.

ca3.title: Cartoon villains with foreign accents drive language bias, Canadian study finds
ca3.description: When popular villains in cartoon shows and movies speak in foreign-accented English, the young children watching the conniving depictions also seem to pick up language biases, Canadian researchers say.

ca3.title: Rainfall helping crews fight wildfires near Labrador City
ca3.description: There are five active wildfires in Labrador West area, but the closest to communities there — the Walsh River fire — has moved farther away from Labrador City and Wabush.

ca3.title: Experts confirm tornado touched down in southwest Winnipeg on Monday
ca3.description: A tornado touched down in southwestern Winnipeg during Monday night's storm, officials from the Northern Tornadoes Project at Western University have confirmed.

Regulator launches inquiry into contentious fees charged by Rogers, Bell and Telus
ca3.description: The Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission has ordered Canada's three largest telecoms to justify their contentious fees and explain why they shouldn't face fines for apparent federal violations.
